# Best 18650 chargers

**Best overall: XTAR VC4SL, about $32.90**
- It has four independent bays, USB-C with QC3.0 input, and adjustable current from 0.25A to 3A.
- The LCD shows voltage, current, capacity, and internal resistance for each cell. It also has capacity-grading and storage modes.
- It fits 18650s, protected 21700s, and AA/AAA NiMH.
- Drawbacks: it doesn't list LiFePO4 support, and one reviewer saw it occasionally mistake NiMH cells for Li-ion and default to the highest current (3A), so check the setting when you start a charge.
- [Buy / see price: XTAR VC4SL](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/). This is the review page, which links to the price. Other reviews: [1Lumen](https://1lumen.com/battery-charger-review/xtar-vc4sl/), [Stephen Knight](https://www.stephenknightphotography.com/post/charger-review-xtar-vc4sl).

**Fastest, and best if you use LiFePO4: Nitecore UMS4, about $38.95**
- It charges up to 3A in one slot with a QC input, and 1A per slot with all four full.
- It supports Li-ion, LiFePO4, and Ni-MH/Ni-Cd. It has internal-resistance readout, reverse-polarity and short-circuit protection, and overtime protection.
- [Nitecore UMS4 specs](https://www.nitecore.com/mobile-product/ums4). Price is from the [Best Batteries listing](https://us.best-batteries.com/reviews/xtar-vc4sl/).

**Best budget: Tenergy TN270, $18.99**
- It's a simple two-bay charger with reverse-polarity detection, a 12-month warranty, and 30-day returns.
- It charges at only 500 mA per slot, so a 3,000 mAh cell takes about 6–7 hours. It has no USB input and only two bays.
- [Buy: Tenergy TN270](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn270-li-ion-18650-charger). This is an affiliate link, so the site earns a commission at no cost to you. Details are on the [product page](https://dealectric.com/tenergy-tn270-li-ion-18650-charger).

**Another popular option: Keenstone 4-Bay Universal Charger**
- Smashing Robotics named it Editor's Choice, citing 4.6 stars across 4,608 reviews, selectable 500 mA or 1 A per bay, and UL/CE/FCC marks. It said cells can lose charge if left in the bays after termination.
- I didn't get a direct purchase link for it. See the [guide](https://www.smashingrobotics.com/best-18650-battery-chargers/), which links to Amazon.

**Which should you get?**
- For most people, get the XTAR VC4SL.
- If you charge LiFePO4 cells or want maximum speed, get the Nitecore UMS4.
- If you only need to charge a pair of flashlight cells occasionally, the Tenergy TN270 is fine.

Whichever you pick, avoid no-name chargers that don't say how they decide a cell is full, and avoid ones that pair slots. [VoltRated](https://voltrated.com/guides/best-chargers) flags both as risky. Prices change, so confirm at checkout.
